newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes mixed, outright levels dip.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes mixed, outright levels dip.

text.p: North Sea wet markets were mixed with December Brent trading at a premium to Friday's level but few buyers seen for cargoes in other grades, traders said.
"It feels like we have seen the top of this market but on Brent there is a battle going on with this week's dates and it's not easy to see who will win," one refiner said.
This week's dates on the CFD market traded earlier at a firm 25 cent premium over January.
Jan Brent on the IPE traded at 1604 GMT down five cents at $22.72 a barrel. Feb fared better, unchanged at $22.13.
A trader picked up a Dec 14-16 Brent on Monday (maximum size) at Jan Brent +35 cents -- up five cents from Friday.
"But the next bid was around +20 so there seems to be a bit of a discrepancy in the market," another trader said.
A Dec 15-17 Brent was picked up by a refiner at Dated Brent +5 cents. Of the two Brent cargoes in Monday's chains (loading Dec 17-19), one was heard already kept by the equity holder.
In the West African market grades held firm with few December cargoes left unsold, traders said.
Forcados was talked at a premium to Dated Brent of 70/80 cents after a cargo was traded at +72 cents late last week.
The buyer, a Spanish refiner, was reportedly reoffering the cargo at a higher price.
"They took a position assuming things would move higher," said a trader for a European major. "If they can't make a margin they'll take it into their own system."
Lighter grades such as Bonny Light and Brass River was also seen firmer.
"In general, everything is going up," said a Mediterranean trader.
Traders said the January loading programmes for West African crudes were expected around Dec 10.
